# Running one synthetic article through the full flow locally

Read-only research; nothing was run. "Unverified" marks claims the repo does not settle.

## 1. Who fetches the HTML: the API, through Firecrawl

- The pipeline never fetches. `POST /jobs` takes the HTML in the body: `{html, recipe?, job_id, domain}` (`pipeline/src/http/routes.ts:12-17`), capped at `maxHtmlBytes` = 1 MiB (`routes.ts:48`, `pipeline/wrangler.jsonc:31`).
- The API fetches, with one strategy only: a Firecrawl scrape, `formats=["rawHtml","markdown"], proxy="auto"` (`api/app/service/fetch.py:79-95`), invoked from `FetchStep` (`api/app/service/pipeline/steps.py:45-60`). No plain-fetch path exists. `.env.example` still calls Firecrawl a "fallback" to a plain fetch; that text is stale.
- The recipe domain is the host of Firecrawl's final URL (`steps.py:58`, `fetch.py:31-33`). The local DB's latest recipe for that domain rides along with the job (`steps.py:62-65`). A new domain has no recipe, so the author agent runs.
- Consequence: through the API, the synthetic page **must be publicly reachable**, because Firecrawl is a hosted scraper and cannot see `localhost`. That means a public host or a tunnel. Each scrape spends Firecrawl credits (`api/app/config.py:73`). Serving the HTML directly to the API would need a new `Fetcher` (`fetch.py:49-52`), but `FetchStep` hardcodes `FirecrawlFetcher` (`steps.py:51`), so a local-file fetch is a code change.
- Direct `POST /jobs` to the pipeline (section 6) needs no URL at all.

## 2. pipeline/ locally

- `pnpm install`, then `pnpm dev`, which runs `build:bundle && vite dev` (`pipeline/package.json:7`) with the Cloudflare and Flue Vite plugins (`pipeline/vite.config.ts`). The port is not configured in `vite.config.ts`, so it is Vite's default (5173, unverified), **not** wrangler's 8787.
- Secret: `CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY` (`pipeline/worker-configuration.d.ts:17`), read by pi-ai's `cloudflareAIGatewayAuth` together with `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` and `CLOUDFLARE_GATEWAY_ID` (`node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-ai/dist/providers/cloudflare-auth.js:1-33`). Wiring: `pipeline/src/agents/model-provider.ts:43-58`.
- The account and gateway IDs are plain vars in `wrangler.jsonc:23-24`, set to the real account and the `nagara` gateway. The model is `cloudflare-ai-gateway/workers-ai/@cf/zai-org/glm-5.3-flash` (`wrangler.jsonc:22`).
- Locally the key goes in `pipeline/.dev.vars`, which is gitignored (`pipeline/.gitignore`) and **does not exist yet**. There is no `.dev.vars.example`, and no doc mentions any of this.
- Local agent runs still call the real AI Gateway on the real account, so they cost Workers AI usage and appear in the gateway's logs. They write no production state.
- Dynamic Workers run locally through miniflare's Worker Loader (`wrangler.jsonc:6`, `pipeline/src/runtime/run.ts:24-26`). This is proven by `pipeline/test/dynamic-workers-proof.test.ts:9-15`. The recipe CPU limit (`recipeCpuMs`) is **not** enforced locally (`dynamic-workers-proof.test.ts:17-22`).
- Durable Object and Workflow state lives in `pipeline/.wrangler/` (gitignored), separate from production.

async def claim_for_retry(db: AsyncSession, item_id: str) -> bool:
    """Atomically move a failed item back to queued for a retry.

    A single conditional UPDATE is the arbiter, not a read-then-write: it gates on status
    still failed AND retry_count below the cap, and increments retry_count in SQL. So two
    concurrent retries on one item cannot both win — only the first UPDATE finds the
    preconditions still met, the second gets rowcount 0 and the route refuses it. This is
    the same problem the pipeline's guarded write solves for the queued→generating transition;
    mirroring its shape keeps the read-then-write race out of the retry path too, which matters
    because a manual recovery route is exactly where a double-click is plausible. retry_count is
    nullable until the first retry, so the guard and the increment both coalesce NULL to 0.
    """
    result = cast(
        CursorResult,
        await db.execute(
            update(Item)
            .where(
                Item.id == item_id,
                Item.status == ItemStatus.FAILED,
                or_(Item.retry_count.is_(None), Item.retry_count < settings.retry_max),

async def claim_for_retry(db: AsyncSession, item_id: str) -> bool:
    """Atomically move a failed item back to queued for a retry.

    A single conditional UPDATE is the arbiter, not a read-then-write: it gates on status
    still failed AND retry_count below the cap, and increments retry_count in SQL. So two
    concurrent retries on one item cannot both win — only the first UPDATE finds the
    preconditions still met, the second gets rowcount 0 and the route refuses it. This is
    the same problem the pipeline's guarded write solves for the queued→generating transition;
    mirroring its shape keeps the read-then-write race out of the retry path too, which matters
    because a manual recovery route is exactly where a double-click is plausible. retry_count is
    nullable until the first retry, so the guard and the increment both coalesce NULL to 0.
    """
    result = cast(
        CursorResult,
        await db.execute(
            update(Item)
            .where(
                Item.id == item_id,
                Item.status == ItemStatus.FAILED,
                or_(Item.retry_count.is_(None), Item.retry_count < settings.retry_max),
            )
            .values(
                status=ItemStatus.QUEUED,
                queued_at=now_iso(),
                error=None,
                retry_count=func.coalesce(Item.retry_count, 0) + 1,
            )
        ),
    )
    if result.rowcount == 0:
        return False
    await db.commit()
    return True

#4 [paragraph]

B18 fails on two counts: a table with formatted cells leaks raw markdown into the spoken form, and a first-time domain can't finish inside the default 300 s ceiling. Everything else I could check passes. The audio is ready, but nobody has listened to it yet.

**Run.** The pipeline ran locally, and the API used a scratch SQLite in `.scratch/markdown-and-lists/local-data-validate/`. TTS came from the deployed `nagara-tts` app, and the article was served through a cloudflared quick tunnel. I changed no production data and no `api/.env`, and every process I started (API, pipeline, tunnel, file server) is stopped.

| Expectation | Result | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Title is the first unit | PASS | #0 |
| Headings and quotes read as their words, one line per paragraph (nested quote too) | PASS | #3, #8, #11 |
| One line per block, never fused | PASS | #20, #26, #28 |
| Ordered items keep their numbers, honouring `start` | PASS | #22 (1–3), #24 (5–6) |
| Nested list in document order, own inner numbering | PASS | #26 |
| Code block inside a list item is silent, and no code unit comes out of the list | PASS | #28 |
| Image inside a list item is silent | NOT EXERCISED | No list item in this article holds an image |
| Task checkboxes removed, struck word read as a plain word | PASS | #35, #10 |
| Table: header line, then one line per row | PASS | #42, #44 |
| Operators as words, `<software>` read as "software" | PASS | #17 |
| Inline formula comes out as alttext `1/2^n` | PASS | #56 |
| Synthesis input is one string per unit, with newlines | PASS | 61 units, 13:13.65 of audio |
| No leaked markdown markers | **FAIL** | #46, see below |
| Item reaches `ready` inside the default ceiling | **FAIL** | see below |

**The table leak (#46).** Table cells are read from their raw source, so markup the parser would normally clear stays in:
- A link reads as `[RFC tradition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Request_for_Comments)`.
- Single-underscore emphasis stays as `_Pairing on the interface_`.
- A cell that ends in a full stop gets a second one (`from..`).
- The `**bold**` cell does come out clean.

The API already read cells this way before this change, and the docs describe it.

**The ceiling.** The first run failed with `enrichment: no result after 300s`. The local author agent took about 5.5 minutes, and the pipeline job completed 29 s after the ceiling fired. I restarted the API with `NAGARA_QUEUED_CEILING_SECONDS=1200` and called the retry route. It picked up the already-completed job, with no second authoring run, and the item reached `ready`.

**Seen but outside the api/ change:** the recipe emitted the three "•" slide bullets (#37–#39) as separate paragraphs, each starting with a literal "•".

**Report:** `.scratch/markdown-and-lists/reports/validate-api/index.html`. It holds all 61 units with display, spoken form and start time.

**Audio:** `.scratch/markdown-and-lists/reports/validate-api/audio.ogg`. `LISTEN.md` next to it has the timestamps. What to listen for:
- **0:00:** the title, read once, with nothing before it.
- **2:07:** "1. Grug brain considered", with no backslash.
- **2:39:** "code rejection review", with no "tilde".
- **4:47:** "software" and "3 less than 4 and 5 greater than 2".
- **5:53 and 6:17:** numbered lists, the second starting at 5.
- **6:34:** the nested checklist.
- **7:11:** silence where the Python block sits inside the list.

import re from markdown_it import MarkdownIt from markdown_it.token import Token from markdown_it.tree import SyntaxTreeNode _LIST_ITEM = re.compile(r"^\s*([-*+]|\d+\.)\s+") _FENCE = re.compile(r"^[ ]{0,3}(```|~~~)") _HEADING = re.compile(r"^\s*#{1,6}\s+") # CommonMark's inline-HTML tag shape, drawn on markdown-it's own boundary: ``, `
` and # `` are tags to the parser, while `3 < 4`, `<3` and the autolink `` are not. # A tag still present in a unit's markdown is prose the author escaped rather than leaked markup: # the words inside it are the article's own. _TAG_SHAPE = r"]*?)?)\s*/?>" # The spoken strip also takes the escaped form: a table cell is read off the raw inline source, # where the backslash escaping the tag in the display is still sitting in front of it. _SPOKEN_HTML_TAG = re.compile(rf"\\?{_TAG_SHAPE}") # A whole run of one marker character, so `**` between spaces is judged as one marker rather than def sanitize_spoken(text: str) -> str: """Turn any leftover markdown emphasis or code marker that touches text into a space (splitting the fused word or sentence), drop the space a marker left before punctuation, and collapse runs of whitespace within each line, keeping the newlines between lines. The same tail guards two producers: parsed markdown, whose invalid run-in emphasis leaks a literal marker, and the describer's structured output, which a JSON schema cannot forbid a marker from carrying inside its string value. A leaked marker is only ever caught by playing the audio, so both paths run through here. It also reduces an XML-like tagged word to the words inside it (`` → software), escaped or not: escaped is the shape a table cell arrives in, since ``_table_lines`` reads a cell off the raw inline source. What angle brackets are left after that, and the arrows, are operators, read as their words.""" def _table_lines(table: SyntaxTreeNode) -> list[str]: """Linearize a markdown table into a header line and one header-aware line per body row ("Col: value, Col: value.") so it reads instead of speaking pipe characters. Cells carry raw inline markup (a `code` span reads its literal backtick), which the sanitize tail clears along with the rest of the unit.""" header, *body = ( [cell.children[0].content if cell.children else "" for cell in row.children] for section in table.children for row in section.children ) return [ ", ".join(header) + ".", *(", ".join(f"{name}: {cell}" for name, cell in zip(header, row)) + "." for row in body), ] 84:def test_a_table_reads_its_header_line_then_one_line_per_row(): 89:def test_table_cell_inline_code_is_sanitized_from_spoken(): 91: # table runs through the same sanitize tail as every other spoken path. 104:def test_escaped_tagged_word_reads_its_words(): 105: assert to_spoken("We ship \\ to users.") == "We ship software to users." 108:def test_escaped_tag_only_unit_reads_its_word(): 109: assert to_spoken("\\") == "software" 120: ("Set \\ here.", "Set your-api-key here."), 162: assert to_spoken("Ship \\ before the \\ closer.") == "Ship software before the div closer." 169:def test_tagged_word_in_a_table_cell_reads_its_words(): 170: # _table_lines reads a cell off the raw inline source, where the escaping backslash is 172: md = "| Name | Tag |\n| --- | --- |\n| widget | \\ |"

Table cells now read through the same inline walk and sanitize tail as any paragraph, so the link, underscore and doubled full stop leaks from B18 are gone. Checks are green.

**Commit:** `a8b7145` fix(api): read table cells through the inline walk like any paragraph

**What changed:**
- A cell is read the same way a paragraph is: a link reduces to its anchor text, emphasis markers are dropped, and code spans keep their text.
- A row or header line gets a full stop only when it doesn't already end in `.`, `!` or `?`.
- The raw-source cell reading is gone, and so is the escaped-tag special case in `_SPOKEN_HTML_TAG`, since nothing else needed it. The parser already removes the escaping backslash from `\<software>`, so it still reads "software". One test case called `sanitize_spoken` on the literal `Set \<your-api-key> here.`; I removed it because that input no longer occurs. This is why the suite count went from 210 to 209.
- I didn't edit `docs/`, so `docs/technical-design/article-extraction.md` still describes cells being read from raw source with the escaped form accepted. It is now out of date.

**Test:** `test_table_cells_read_through_the_same_inline_walk_as_prose`. The table has `**Design doc first**`, a cell with a link that ends in a full stop, `_Pairing on the interface_`, and a cell holding `\<software>`. It asserts these spoken lines:
```
Practice, Description.
Practice: Design doc first, Description: See the RFC tradition it borrows from.
Practice: Pairing on the interface, Description: Two engineers argue about software first.
```
The existing table tests still pass, including the inline code cell and the tagged word in prose.

**Checks:**
```
ruff check → All checks passed!
ty check   → All checks passed!
pytest     → 209 passed, 6 warnings in 6.32s
```
